name: Question 17
problem:
Suppose $n=-8p+2q+7,$ where $p,q\in Z.$ Complete the following argument.

The number $n$ is {{field-1}} since 

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =-8p+2q+7 \\  & =2(-4p+{{field-2}})+1 \\  & ={{field-3}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $a=${{field-4}}.
worked_solution:
An integer is *odd* if it can be written as $2a+1,$ where $a$ is an integer.

Now, note the following regarding the expression $-8p+2q+7:$

- All terms, apart from the constant term, have a common factor of $2.$

- The constant term can be written as $7=6+1.$

Therefore, we complete our argument as follows:

The number $n$ is $\text{odd}$ since

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =-8p+2q+7 \\  & =(-8p+2q+6)+1 \\  & =2({{-4p+q+3}_{⏟}}_{a})+1 \\  & =2a+1,\end{aligned}
$$

where $a=-4p+q+3\in Z.$
